title: AVO7-Part-4
description: 70-question exam covering gyroscopes, gyro horizons, erection systems, RLGs, turn-and-bank/turn coordinators, and rate gyros.

questions.question: In gyro horizon pitch up
options: A. aircraft symbol below horizontal bar
B. aircraft symbol aligned with horizon bar
C. aircraft symbol above horizontal bar
questions.explanation: The gyro horizon shows pitch using the aircraft symbol relative to the stabilized horizon bar.

questions.question: Purpose of air blows on the bucket
questions.explanation: Air is directed into the gyro rotor buckets to spin the pneumatic gyro.

questions.question: Pneumatic gyro spin
options: A. electrical current through the gimbal
B. gravity acting on the rotor
C. air blows on the bucket
questions.explanation: Pneumatic gyro rotation is produced by air blown through nozzles onto the rotor buckets.

questions.question: Torque leveling switch connection
questions.explanation: The supplied answer is retained from the exam source; the module describes the electrical leveling-switch and torque-motor control connections.

questions.question: What spins a gyro
questions.explanation: Gyroscopic flight-instrument rotors are driven by pneumatic or electrical methods.

questions.question: Latitude effect on free gyro drift
options: A. drift decreases at higher latitude
C. drift increases at higher latitude
questions.explanation: Apparent drift is related to Earth's rotation and latitude; the supplied exam answer is preserved.

questions.question: Device preventing false indication due to acceleration
questions.explanation: Erection cutout prevents gravity-controlled erection systems from responding incorrectly to acceleration/turning forces.

questions.question: Effect of gimbal error
questions.explanation: Gimbal error can cause incorrect instrument indications because the gimbal system is displaced from its proper geometry.

questions.question: Component driving horizon bar
options: C. separate pitch and roll servomotor
questions.explanation: The supplied answer is retained from the exam source for the horizon-bar drive arrangement.

questions.question: Removing gyro while spinning
questions.explanation: Gyroscopic instruments can suffer internal damage if removed while still spinning.

questions.question: Gyroscope with vertical spin axis
questions.explanation: A vertical gyroscope has its spin axis arranged vertically to establish an attitude reference.

questions.question: Gyro flag not disappearing
questions.explanation: The supplied answer identifies a sticking flag condition.

questions.question: RLG rotation measured when frequency
questions.explanation: RLG rotation is detected from the frequency difference between counter-rotating laser beams.

questions.question: Remotely vertical gyros send to
questions.explanation: Remote vertical gyros provide reference information to flight director/automatic flight-control and instrument systems.

questions.question: Roll reference rigid
options: B. rotor, outer gimbal, inner gimbal
questions.explanation: The supplied answer identifies the rigid roll-reference arrangement.

questions.question: Pitch reference rigid
questions.explanation: The supplied answer identifies the rigid pitch-reference arrangement.

questions.question: Incorrect statement
options: A. Ball type erection system can be used on electrical gyro
B. Dry pumps require no lubrication
C. RLG uses beams traveling in opposite directions
questions.explanation: The exam marks this as the incorrect statement. The module separately describes ball erection and the electrical leveling-switch/torque-motor system.

questions.question: Ball erection system
options: A. balls displaced & create unbalanced weight
B. balls remain fixed and create no force
questions.explanation: Gravity displaces the balls in the rotating holder, shifting their mass and producing corrective precession.

questions.question: Acceleration error
questions.explanation: Acceleration can displace gravity-controlled erection devices and produce a false pitch indication.

questions.question: Vertical gyro spins about
questions.explanation: The vertical gyro uses a vertical spin axis for its reference.

questions.question: Angular change 90 degree away
questions.explanation: Precession is the angular change in the plane of rotation produced by an applied force, occurring 90° away in the direction of rotation.

questions.question: Freedom about axis perpendicular through center
questions.explanation: Spinning freedom is freedom about the spin axis through the rotor center.

questions.question: Rotor canted upward 30 degree
questions.explanation: The supplied answer is retained from the exam source.

questions.question: Turn & bank indicator shows
options: B. rate of turn and slip indication
questions.explanation: A turn-and-bank indicator provides rate-of-turn and slip/bank information.

questions.question: Number of rate gyros for 3 axes
questions.explanation: The supplied answer is three rate gyros for the three aircraft axes.

questions.question: Incorrect statement
options: A. Dry pumps are light in weight and require lubrication
B. Dry pumps require no lubrication
C. Wet pumps use engine oil for lubrication
questions.explanation: The exam marks this as the incorrect statement. The module says dry pumps are lighter and require no lubrication.

questions.question: Incorrect statement
options: A. RLGs have long service life
B. Ring laser gyros are rugged and have short service life
C. RLGs have moving mechanical vanes
questions.explanation: The exam marks this as the incorrect statement. The module says RLGs are rugged and have a long service life.

questions.question: Fast erection switch effect
questions.explanation: Fast erection switches the torque-motor supply to full line voltage, increasing current and erection torque.

questions.question: Correct statement
options: A. Ring laser gyro uses a beam of light
questions.explanation: An RLG uses laser light beams traveling around a closed cavity.

questions.question: Instrument indicating pitch & bank
questions.explanation: The gyro horizon indicates aircraft pitch and bank attitude.

questions.question: Correct about rate gyro
options: A. requires a pendulous vane erection system
B. requires a ball erection system
questions.explanation: A rate gyro uses spring restraint and does not require an erection system like a vertical attitude gyro.

questions.question: Purpose of erection system in vertical gyro
options: B. erect to longitudinal & vertical position
questions.explanation: The erection system brings the gyro toward its required reference position and maintains it.

questions.question: Remotely vertical gyro supplies reference
questions.explanation: Remote vertical gyro outputs are used by automatic flight-control and instrument systems.

questions.question: Instrument controlled by gyroscope
questions.explanation: The attitude indicator is a gyroscopic flight instrument.

questions.question: Freedom of gyro rotor about vertical axis
questions.explanation: Veering freedom is freedom about the vertical axis.

questions.question: Gyroscope of turn-and-bank indicator contains
questions.explanation: The supplied answer is retained exactly from the exam source.

questions.question: Device for attitude displacement pickup
questions.explanation: Synchro systems can pick up and transmit attitude displacement information.

questions.question: Maximum suction/pressure for directional & vertical gyro
questions.explanation: The pneumatic gyro horizon and directional gyro require 4 inches of mercury suction according to the module.

questions.question: RLG installation
options: A. one unit for the entire aircraft only
C. only on the vertical axis
questions.explanation: An RLG is installed for each aircraft axis of flight.

questions.question: Incorrect about RLG
options: A. beams travel in opposite directions
B. beams travel same direction around cavity
C. frequency difference is used to measure rotation
questions.explanation: The exam marks this as incorrect because the two RLG laser beams travel in opposite directions.

questions.question: Rotor speed >4000 rpm unnecessary
options: A. because rigidity increases with speed
B. because it will precess after force applied
C. because the rotor would stop immediately
questions.explanation: The supplied answer is retained exactly from the exam source.

questions.question: Incorrect statement
options: A. plane of rotation is vertical
B. vertical gyro has a vertical spin axis
C. plane of rotation of vertical gyro is horizontal
questions.explanation: The supplied statement is the exam's marked incorrect statement; the module identifies the vertical gyro by its vertical spin axis.

questions.question: Piezoelectric dithering motor prevents lock-in
questions.explanation: The piezoelectric dithering motor prevents RLG lock-in at low rotational speeds.

questions.question: Factor affecting ball erection
options: A. unbalance in rotor weight distribution
questions.explanation: Ball erection depends on the displacement of ball mass and the resulting unbalance/precessional force.

questions.question: Freedom of gyro rotor about horizontal axis
questions.explanation: Tilting freedom is freedom about a horizontal axis at right angles to the spin axis.

questions.question: Pitch reference rigid system
options: B. outer gimbal and case only
C. case and bank pointer only
questions.explanation: The supplied answer is retained exactly from the exam source.

questions.question: Purpose of cathode/anodes in RLG
options: A. create potential difference for ions
questions.explanation: The supplied answer is retained from the exam; it concerns the electrical operation of the RLG laser medium.

questions.question: Pitch level switches send signal to
questions.explanation: The supplied answer is retained from the exam source for the pitch leveling-switch circuit.

questions.question: Signals generated in synchros transmitted to
questions.explanation: Synchro signals are transmitted to flight-control and instrument systems.

questions.question: Leveling switch sends signal to
questions.explanation: The supplied answer is retained from the exam source.

questions.question: Rate gyro doesn’t require erection
options: B. uses a ball erection system
questions.explanation: A rate gyro is spring restrained and therefore does not need a separate erection system.

questions.question: Coordinated turn indication
options: C. ball remains centered in inclinometer
questions.explanation: In a coordinated turn, the inclinometer ball remains centered.

questions.question: Rotor canted upward 30 degree
questions.explanation: The supplied answer is retained exactly from the exam source.

questions.question: Purpose of erection system in vertical gyro
questions.explanation: The erection system restores the vertical gyro to its vertical position.

questions.question: Number of gimbals in turn & bank
questions.explanation: The turn-and-bank rate gyro described in the module has a single gimbal.

questions.question: Error when gyro loses spin axis
questions.explanation: Gimbal lock occurs when the gyro loses its useful attitude reference because of gimbal orientation.

questions.question: RLG operation based on
questions.explanation: RLG operation uses the Sagnac effect, in which rotation produces a measurable difference between counter-rotating light beams.

questions.question: Rate gyro principle
questions.explanation: Rate gyros operate using gyroscopic precession.

questions.question: Purpose of pressure sealing in electrical vertical gyro
questions.explanation: Pressure sealing prevents moisture from entering the electrical vertical gyro.

questions.question: Gyro horizon in level flight
options: A. aircraft symbol aligns with horizon bar
B. aircraft symbol is always above the bar
C. aircraft symbol is always below the bar
questions.explanation: In level flight, the aircraft symbol aligns with the stabilized horizon bar.

questions.question: Erection cut-out occurs when bank angle >
questions.explanation: Erection cutout operates automatically when the aircraft banks more than 10 degrees.

questions.question: Erection of vertical gyro brings back to
questions.explanation: Erection restores the vertical gyro to its vertical reference axis.

questions.question: Gyro rotates out of plane
options: A. air ports remain exactly equal
C. electrical current stops the rotor
questions.explanation: When the pneumatic gyro rotates out of plane, unequal airflow through the ports produces the corrective erection force.

questions.question: Correct statement
options: A. Pitch & roll signals from vertical gyro sent to indicator servomotor
B. only yaw signals are sent
C. signals are sent only to the fuel system
questions.explanation: The supplied answer describes the pitch and roll signal path from the vertical gyro to the indicator servomotor.

questions.question: Erection mechanism uses
questions.explanation: The module states that erection systems generally use mechanical and electrical methods.

questions.question: Ways of producing airflow over gyro wheel
questions.explanation: Airflow over pneumatic gyro wheels can be produced by suction or pressure.

questions.question: Vertical gyro driven by
questions.explanation: The supplied answer is retained exactly from the exam source for the stated vertical-gyro drive.

questions.question: Incorrect statement
options: A. Rotor is oriented in the horizontal plane
B. Rotor of gyro horizon oriented in vertical plane
C. The rotor is driven by an electric motor in an electric gyro
questions.explanation: The exam marks this as incorrect; the module states that the electric attitude-indicator rotor remains oriented in the horizontal plane.

questions.question: In pitch-bank compensation
options: A. roll switch is always connected during turn
B. roll switch disconnected during turn
C. pitch switch is removed during turn
questions.explanation: In pitch-bank erection, the roll/bank switch is disconnected during a turn and the pitch leveling switch controls the erection system.

questions.question: Vertical gyro system attitude change
options: A. signals flow only from the magnetic compass
B. signals flow only from fuel quantity sensors
C. signals flow from pitch & roll synchros
questions.explanation: The supplied answer describes the pitch/roll synchro signal flow for vertical gyro attitude changes.
